mainTopic: Taking wood from a סוכה on יום טוב: סותר אהל, רבי שמעון and מוקצה, and whether a תנאי works on a סוכה של מצוה
overview: The משנה says you may not take wood from a סוכה on יום טוב, only from what is near it. The גמרא asks why 'near it' is not also סותר אהל. שמואל answers that it means loose wood leaning on the walls, and רב מנשיא answers that it means tied bundles that never became part of the roof. A ברייתא adds that רבי שמעון permits taking wood even from the סוכה itself. The גמרא explains that he is talking about a shaky סוכה that has already fallen, so there is no סותר אהל, and he does not hold of מוקצה. The ברייתא also says that a תנאי can permit a סוכה built for the חג. The גמרא objects that a סוכה של מצוה is holy 'for ה׳' all seven days, so it limits the תנאי to an ordinary hut. A תנאי on decorations works only because it stops holiness from ever starting at בין השמשות. Finally, the גמרא explains that the סוכה's holiness lasts all seven days, unlike an אתרוג, because the מצוה of סוכה continues through the nights and makes the חג one long day.

steps.title: The משנה: no wood from the סוכה, only from near it
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that on יום טוב one may not take wood from a סוכה, but may take wood from what is near it.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: We may not take wood from the סוכה, but only from what is near it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a simple rule: on יום טוב you cannot pull wood off a סוכה to use for cooking, but you can take wood that is near the סוכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה does not say why taking from the סוכה is forbidden. It also does not say exactly what 'near it' means. The גמרא will now ask about both of these points.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה (the base text we are learning)
A booth / hut covered with סכך
What is near it / next to it

steps.confusionAlert: This משנה is not only about סוכות. The rule applies on any יום טוב, for example a סוכה still standing from before.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ אֵין נוֹטְלִין עֵצִים מִן הַסּוּכָּה,
phrases.english: MISHNAH: We may not take wood from the sukkah,
phrases.notes: Meaning: on יום טוב.

phrases.english: but only from what is near it.
phrases.notes: What exactly 'near it' means is the subject of the גמרא.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wood may not be taken from a סוכה on יום טוב, but may be taken from what is near it.

steps.title: Why is 'near it' different? It also breaks down a tent
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה: if taking from the סוכה is forbidden because of סותר אהל, then taking from near it should also be סותר אהל.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is different about taking from the סוכה, that it is not allowed? Because one is breaking down a tent. But taking from near it also breaks down a tent!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the משנה treats the two cases differently. It assumes the reason for the איסור is breaking down a tent (סותר אהל), and that reason seems to apply to both cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא first gives the reason for the first half of the משנה: removing wood from a סוכה is סותר אהל. Then it asks: wood 'near' the סוכה seems to be part of the same structure, so removing it should also be סותר אהל. We now need a definition of 'near it' that is not part of the tent.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmudic discussion on the משנה

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ מַאי שְׁנָא מִן הַסּוּכָּה דְּלָא —
phrases.english: GEMARA: What is different about taking from the sukkah, that it is not allowed?
phrases.notes: This opens the question.

phrases.english: Because he is breaking down a tent.
phrases.notes: The assumed reason for the איסור.

phrases.english: But from what is near it also —
he is breaking down a tent!
phrases.notes: So why does the משנה permit it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the distinction drawn in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's permission to take wood 'from near it'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the איסור is סותר אהל, then wood near the סוכה (seemingly part of it) should be forbidden for the same reason.

steps.title: שמואל: 'near it' means wood leaning against the walls
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of שמואל explains that 'near it' means wood placed next to the walls. That wood is not part of the סוכה itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: What does 'near it' mean? Near the walls.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers the question by defining 'near it.' It means wood that is leaning against the walls of the סוכה, not wood that is part of the סוכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wood leaning against the walls was never built into the structure. So removing it does not break down any tent. The walls and the roof themselves remain forbidden.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
phrases.notes: Attribution line.

phrases.english: What is 'near'? Near the walls.
phrases.notes: Loose wood resting beside the walls, not part of the structure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: מַאי סָמוּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא by redefining 'near it'.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefinition of the case (אוקימתא) in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Near it' seemed to mean wood that is part of the סוכה structure, so removing it would be סותר אהל.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Near it' means loose wood leaning against the walls. Removing it is not סותר אהל.

steps.title: רב מנשיא: even wood on the roof is fine if it is in tied bundles
steps.stepSummary: רב מנשיא answers differently: even wood not near the walls, lying on the roof, may be taken if it is in tied bundles, because bundles never became part of the roof.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מנשיא said: You can even say it is talking about wood that is not near the walls. When that teaching was taught, it was about bundles.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מנשיא gives a second answer. 'Near it' can even mean wood up on the סוכה roof, as long as it is still tied in bundles.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tied bundles of reeds lying on the סוכה were never opened and spread out as part of the roof. So they are only resting there, and taking them does not break down the tent. This answer allows a wider case than שמואל's: the wood can even be on top of the סוכה.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who gives an alternative answer

steps.confusionAlert: רב מנשיא is not saying roof wood is generally permitted. Only bundles that were never untied are permitted, because they never became part of the roof.

phrases.english: Rav Menashya said:
phrases.notes: Attribution line.

phrases.english: You can even say it refers to wood that is not near the walls,
phrases.notes: For example, lying on the roof.

phrases.english: when that teaching was taught, it was about bundles.
phrases.notes: Tied bundles are not part of the סכך.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב מְנַשְּׁיָא אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא בְּשֶׁאֵין סָמוּךְ לַדְּפָנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to the same קשיא, different from שמואל's.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative אוקימתא: the wood is in bundles
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Wood not next to the walls (on the roof) would seem to be part of the tent.
steps.terutzMaskana: Tied bundles are not part of the roof, so taking them is not סותר אהל, even from on top of the סוכה.

steps.title: A ברייתא: רבי שמעון permits taking from the sukkah
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר יוסף teaches a ברייתא before רבי יוחנן. It repeats the משנה's rule and adds that רבי שמעון permits taking wood even from the סוכה itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר יוסף taught before רבי יוחנן: We may not take wood from the סוכה, but only from what is near it. And רבי שמעון permits.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that shows the משנה is a מחלוקת. The משנה's view is the תנא קמא, and רבי שמעון disagrees and permits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now we learn that the משנה's rule is not unanimous. רבי שמעון allows taking wood even from the סוכה itself. His reason is not stated here, but Steps 7–11 explain it: he does not hold of מוקצה, and the case is a shaky סוכה that has fallen.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא, often lenient on מוקצה

steps.confusionAlert: The first half of this ברייתא repeats the משנה word for word. The new information is only רבי שמעון's lenient opinion.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר יוֹסֵף קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Yosef taught before Rabbi Yochanan:
phrases.notes: Introduces a ברייתא.

phrases.english: We may not take wood from the sukkah
phrases.notes: Same wording as the משנה.

phrases.english: but only from what is near it,
and Rabbi Shimon permits.
phrases.notes: Even from the סוכה itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר יוֹסֵף קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that reveals a dissenting view on the משנה's rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תנא קמא forbids taking wood from the סוכה. רבי שמעון permits it.

steps.title: Everyone agrees: a סוכה built for סוכות is forbidden during the festival, unless a condition was made
steps.stepSummary: Even רבי שמעון agrees that a סוכה built for the חג may not be used for wood during the חג. If the owner made a תנאי beforehand, it all depends on his condition.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they agree that a סוכה built for the festival is forbidden during the festival. And if he made a condition about it, everything follows his condition.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with a point of agreement and an exception. A סוכה made for סוכות is forbidden during סוכות according to everyone, but a תנאי made beforehand can change that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A סוכה used for the מצוה during the חג is set aside for its holy purpose, so even רבי שמעון forbids taking from it. On its surface, the ברייתא adds that a תנאי made in advance lets the owner keep using it. The גמרא will question this in Step 12, and in Step 14 it limits the תנאי to an ordinary hut, not a סוכה של מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: They agree (both sides of the מחלוקת)
A סוכה built for the festival of סוכות

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה forbids taking wood from a סוכה but permits wood 'near it.' According to שמואל this means wood leaning on the walls; according to רב מנשיא it means tied bundles, even on the roof. רבי שמעון permits even from the סוכה, but everyone forbids a סוכת החג during the חג. The ברייתא adds that a תנאי helps, but Step 14 limits that to an ordinary hut.
steps.whyThisMatters: This line about a תנאי is the target of the next discussion (Steps 12–16). There the גמרא concludes that a תנאי works only for an ordinary hut or for decorations, and never for the wood of a סוכה של מצוה.

phrases.english: And they agree regarding a festival sukkah during the festival, that it is forbidden.
phrases.notes: Even רבי שמעון agrees.

phrases.english: And if he made a condition about it —
phrases.notes: Before the festival, when he built or designated it.

phrases.english: everything follows his condition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא, adding a point of agreement and an exception through a תנאי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A סוכה built for the חג is forbidden during the חג according to everyone, unless a תנאי was made, in which case the condition decides.

steps.title: How can רבי שמעון allow taking down part of a structure?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא: how can רבי שמעון permit taking wood from the סוכה itself, when doing so is סותר אהל?
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי שמעון really permit this? But the person is taking apart a tent!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is surprised by רבי שמעון's opinion in the ברייתא. Pulling wood off a standing סוכה means taking apart a structure, and that is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the reason for forbidding wood from the סוכה was סותר אהל, which is a building-type prohibition. מוקצה is a different issue. Even someone who is lenient about מוקצה should still forbid taking apart a structure, so רבי שמעון's leniency seems impossible.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so that... (introduces a challenge)
A tent or structure (Aramaic form of אֹהֶל)

phrases.english: And does Rabbi Shimon permit it?
phrases.notes: Said with surprise. This refers to the ברייתא in Step 5.

phrases.english: But he is taking apart a tent!
phrases.notes: The same reason used against the משנה in Step 2.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מַתִּיר? וְהָא קָא סָתַר אֻהְלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רבי שמעון's lenient view from the ברייתא in Step 5 and attacks it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's ruling that a person may take wood from the סוכה itself.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Taking wood from a standing סוכה is סותר אהל, and that prohibition has nothing to do with מוקצה. So even רבי שמעון should forbid it.

steps.title: The case is a fallen סוכה, and רבי שמעון rejects מוקצה
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק explains that the ברייתא is talking about a סוכה that already fell. רבי שמעון is lenient because he does not hold of מוקצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: Here we are dealing with a סוכה that fell down. רבי שמעון follows his usual reasoning, because he does not hold of מוקצה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers the challenge by changing the case. The סוכה has already collapsed, so nobody is taking apart a standing structure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the סוכה has fallen, the problem of סותר אהל disappears. The only remaining question is whether the wood is מוקצה, since it was not ready for use before יום טוב. רבי שמעון holds there is no מוקצה, so he permits it.

keyTerms.meaning: We are dealing with (sets up which case is meant)
Something set aside from use, which may not be used on שבת or יום טוב

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
Here we are dealing with a sukka that fell down,
phrases.notes: Since it is already down, nothing is being taken apart.

phrases.english: and Rabbi Shimon follows his own reasoning,
since he does not hold of muktzeh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 7 by moving the case to a סוכה that already collapsed.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רבי שמעון allowed taking wood from a standing סוכה, which would be סותר אהל.
steps.terutzMaskana: He is talking about a fallen סוכה. The only issue there is מוקצה, and he does not hold of מוקצה.

steps.title: Proof that רבי שמעון rejects מוקצה: leftover lamp oil
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי שמעון permits leftover oil from a lamp that went out on שבת, while the תנא קמא forbids it as מוקצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: the leftover oil in a lamp or in a bowl is forbidden. But רבי שמעון permits it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to back up the claim that רבי שמעון does not hold of מוקצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lamp was burning when שבת began, so its oil was set aside from use. When the lamp goes out, the leftover oil would normally be מוקצה. רבי שמעון still permits it, and that matches his leniency about the wood of a fallen סוכה.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
Bowl (placed under the lamp to catch oil)

phrases.english: As it was taught: the leftover oil in the lamp
and in the bowl is forbidden.
phrases.notes: This is the view of the תנא קמא, who holds of מוקצה.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon permits it.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: תירוץ (part of the answer in Step 8)
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the claim in Step 8 that רבי שמעון does not hold of מוקצה.
steps.raayaObject: רבי שמעון does not hold of מוקצה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about leftover lamp oil on שבת.

steps.title: A lamp is expected to go out, but a סוכה is not expected to fall
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the comparison. A person expects his lamp to go out, but he does not sit around expecting his סוכה to fall.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are the cases really alike? There, a person sits and waits for his lamp to go out. Here, does a person sit and wait for his סוכה to fall?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from the lamp oil. It says the two cases are not the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון's leniency works only when the person had the thing in mind before יום טוב. A lamp always goes out eventually, so the owner already planned to use the leftover oil. A sturdy סוכה is not expected to fall, so its wood was never in the owner's mind, and even רבי שמעון might call it מוקצה.

keyTerms.meaning: Are the cases really alike? (rejects a comparison)

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying that רבי שמעון does hold of מוקצה. It is saying that his leniency covers only things a person expected to use. A sturdy סוכה falling is something no one expects.

phrases.english: Is it comparable?
There, a person sits and waits
for when his lamp will go out,
but here, does a person sit and wait
for when his sukka will fall?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי דָּמֵי? הָתָם אָדָם יוֹשֵׁב וּמְצַפֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in Step 9, and so undercuts the answer in Step 8.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The comparison between the lamp oil and a fallen סוכה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: With the lamp, the owner expected it to go out. With a סוכה, the owner never expected it to fall, so his mind was never on its wood.

steps.title: The case is a shaky סוכה the owner expected might fall
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק narrows the case further: a shaky סוכה, which the owner already thought might fall since before יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: Here we are dealing with a shaky סוכה, where since yesterday his mind was on it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק fixes the problem raised in Step 10 by saying the סוכה was shaky to begin with.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the סוכה was weak, the owner expected before יום טוב that it might fall, and he had its wood in mind. That makes it just like the lamp, so רבי שמעון's rejection of מוקצה applies.

keyTerms.meaning: His mind was on it (he expected to use it)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי שמעון, wood from a סוכה may be taken on יום טוב only when the סוכה has already fallen (so there is no סותר אהל) and it was shaky to begin with (so the owner had it in mind and it is not מוקצה).

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
Here we are dealing with a shaky sukka,
where since yesterday his mind was on it.
phrases.notes: Before יום טוב, he already expected it might fall.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the rejection in Step 10 by narrowing the case to a shaky סוכה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A סוכה falling is unexpected, so its wood would be מוקצה even for רבי שמעון.
steps.terutzMaskana: A shaky סוכה was expected to fall, so the owner's mind was on its wood, just like the lamp oil.

steps.title: Can a condition work for a סוכה used for the מצוה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's rule about a סוכת החג again and asks whether a תנאי can actually take effect on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא said: All agree that a סוכה built for the חג is forbidden during the חג, but if he made a condition on it, it all follows his condition. Does a condition really work for it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the last line of the ברייתא from Step 6 and questions it. The next step brings the sources behind the question, and Step 14 answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 said a תנאי decides the outcome. Here the גמרא doubts that. A סוכה used for the מצוה has a special holiness during the חג, so maybe a person cannot use a תנאי to keep the right to use its wood.

keyTerms.meaning: A סוכה built for the מצוה of the festival

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new ruling. The גמרא is quoting the ברייתא from Step 6 word for word so that it can challenge the idea of a תנאי.

phrases.english: And all agree regarding a sukka of the festival
that during the festival it is forbidden,
but if he made a condition on it,
it all goes according to his condition.
And does a condition work for it?
phrases.notes: This is the actual challenge. The next step brings the sources behind it, and Step 14 answers it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רבי שמעון discussion and goes back to the end of the ברייתא (Step 6) to question it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's statement that a תנאי works for a סוכת החג.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A סוכה used for the מצוה may carry a holiness that a private condition cannot remove, so the תנאי should not work.

steps.title: The wood of a סוכה is holy for all seven days
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא backs up its question with two sources. They show that the wood of a סוכה is forbidden all seven days, because the סוכה is "for ה׳" just like the חגיגה offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רב ששת said in the name of רבי עקיבא: Where do we learn that the wood of a סוכה is forbidden all seven days? From the verse "The festival of סוכות, seven days, for ה׳." And a ברייתא teaches that רבי יהודה בן בתירא says: Where do we learn that just as Heaven's name rests on the חגיגה offering, it also rests on the סוכה? From the verse "The festival of סוכות, seven days, for ה׳." Just as the festival offering is for ה׳, the סוכה is also for ה׳.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is backing up the question from Step 12. It brings two sources showing that the wood of a סוכה is holy and forbidden all seven days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא learns from the verse that the wood of a סוכה is forbidden all seven days. רבי יהודה בן בתירא explains why: the verse compares the סוכה to the חגיגה offering, so the סוכה carries a kind of holiness. If the wood is holy like a קרבן, a person should not be able to cancel that holiness with a simple תנאי.

keyTerms.meaning: The wood (building materials) of the סוכה
The name of Heaven, meaning holiness or dedication to ה׳
The festival peace-offering brought on the רגלים

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new question. It is the proof behind the question already asked in Step 12: "Can a תנאי really work on a סוכת החג?"
steps.whyThisMatters: The idea that the סוכה is "for ה׳" is the source for the rule that you may not use the סוכה's wood for anything else during סוכות.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא:
phrases.english: But didn't Rav Sheshet say in the name of Rabbi Akiva:
From where do we know that the wood of a sukkah
is forbidden all seven days?
As it says: "The festival of Sukkot, seven days, for ה׳."

phrases.aramaic: וְתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָא אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: And a baraita teaches: Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira says:

phrases.aramaic: מִנַּיִן שֶׁכְּשֵׁם שֶׁחָל שֵׁם שָׁמַיִם עַל הַחֲגִיגָה,
phrases.english: From where do we know that just as Heaven's name takes effect on the festival offering,

phrases.aramaic: כָּךְ חָל שֵׁם שָׁמַיִם עַל הַסּוּכָּה —
phrases.english: so too Heaven's name takes effect on the sukkah?

phrases.aramaic: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״חַג הַסּוּכּוֹת שִׁבְעַת יָמִים לַה׳״,
phrases.english: The verse teaches: "The festival of Sukkot, seven days, for ה׳."

phrases.aramaic: מָה חַג לַה׳ — אַף סוּכָּה לַה׳.
phrases.english: Just as the festival offering is for ה׳, so too the sukkah is for ה׳.
phrases.notes: חַג here refers to the חגיגה offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the sources behind the question raised in Step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's statement that a תנאי works on a סוכת החג.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The wood of a סוכה is holy like a קרבן and forbidden for seven days, so a private תנאי should not be able to remove that status.

steps.title: The end of the ברייתא is about an ordinary hut
steps.stepSummary: רב מנשיא בריה דרבא says the ending of the ברייתא, which allows a תנאי, is talking about an everyday סוכה, not a סוכה built for the מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מנשיא, son of רבא, said: The last part of the ברייתא is talking about an ordinary סוכה. But for a סוכה built for the מצוה, a תנאי does not work.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מנשיא answers the question by limiting the case. The rule that a תנאי helps applies only to a regular, everyday hut.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this answer, it seemed the ברייתא allowed a תנאי even on a סוכה של מצוה. Now the ending (סיפא) is understood as a different case: a hut used all year round, which has no holiness. A סוכה של מצוה stays holy, and no תנאי can change that.

keyTerms.meaning: The last part of a משנה or ברייתא
We have arrived at (switched to) a different case
An ordinary hut, not built for the מצוה
A סוכה built for the מצוה of the חג
It does not work or take effect

phrases.english: Rav Menashya, son of Rava, said:
In the latter clause we have come to an ordinary sukkah,
but a sukkah of מצוה
a condition does not work on it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב מְנַשְּׁיָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא סֵיפָא אֲתָאן לְסוּכָּה דְעָלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Steps 12–13 by reassigning the ending of the ברייתא to a different case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the ברייתא: the סיפא is about a different case (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא allows a תנאי even on a סוכה של מצוה.
steps.terutzMaskana: A תנאי works only on an ordinary hut. On a סוכה של מצוה it has no effect.

steps.title: A ברייתא allows a condition on סוכה decorations
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב מנשיא. A ברייתא says the decorations of a properly built סוכה are forbidden until after the חג, but if the owner made a תנאי, everything follows his תנאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does a תנאי really not work on a סוכה של מצוה? But a ברייתא teaches: If someone covered his סוכה properly with סכך, and decorated it with embroidered cloths and patterned sheets, and hung nuts, almonds, peaches, pomegranates, bunches of grapes, wines, oils, flours, and wreaths of grain stalks in it, he may not use them until after the last day of the חג. But if he made a תנאי about them, everything follows his תנאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב מנשיא's answer. It quotes a ברייתא about a real סוכה של מצוה where a תנאי does work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא clearly describes a סוכה של מצוה, since it was built "כהלכתה," properly by the rules. Yet it says a תנאי works on the decorations. This seems to contradict רב מנשיא's claim that a תנאי never works on a סוכה של מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: He covered it with סכך properly, according to הלכה
To take or use something from them

steps.confusionAlert: This ברייתא is about the decorations hanging in the סוכה, not the סוכה's wood or walls. That difference is the key to the next answer.

phrases.english: And for a sukkah of מצוה, a condition does not work?
But it is taught: If he roofed it properly
and decorated it with embroidered cloths and patterned sheets,

phrases.aramaic: וְתָלָה בָּהּ אֱגוֹזִים שְׁקֵדִים אֲפַרְסְקִים וְרִמּוֹנִים
phrases.english: and hung in it nuts, almonds, peaches, and pomegranates
and bunches of grapes,
wines, oils, fine flours, and wreaths of grain stalks
it is forbidden to take from them

phrases.aramaic: עַד מוֹצָאֵי יוֹם טוֹב הָאַחֲרוֹן שֶׁל חַג.
phrases.english: until after the last festival day of the Chag.
But if he made a condition about them,
everything follows his condition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב מנשיא's answer in Step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב מנשיא's claim that a תנאי does not work on a סוכה של מצוה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא about a properly built סוכה של מצוה says a תנאי does work on its decorations.

steps.title: Decorations can be excluded, but the wood becomes holy
steps.stepSummary: אביי ורבא explain that the ברייתא's תנאי works because the owner said in advance he would not set the decorations aside during בין השמשות, so no holiness ever came onto them. The wood of the סוכה itself does become holy and is מוקצה for all seven days.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי and רבא both say: The ברייתא is talking about someone who says, "I am not separating myself from them during the whole of בין השמשות," so holiness never takes hold of them. But the wood of the סוכה, which does become holy, is set aside (מוקצה) for all seven days.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי ורבא answer the challenge. A תנאי can stop holiness from starting on the decorations, but it cannot help the wood, which becomes holy just by being part of the סוכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנאי for the decorations works by preventing holiness from ever taking hold at בין השמשות, the moment the חג begins. It does not remove holiness after it has already started. The wood of the סוכה is different: it becomes holy no matter what, so it stays forbidden all seven days, and this supports רב מנשיא.

keyTerms.meaning: I am not separating myself from them (I keep the right to use them)
Twilight, the moment the יום טוב begins
It became מוקצה (set aside from use)

steps.whatToRemember: A תנאי can stop holiness from starting on סוכה decorations if he declares it before בין השמשות. The wood of a סוכה של מצוה becomes holy anyway and is forbidden all seven days, and no תנאי helps.
steps.confusionAlert: The תנאי does not "cancel" holiness. It works only because it prevents holiness from ever starting on the decorations.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the practical practice of making a תנאי on סוכה decorations before the חג. It also explains why the סוכה's walls and סכך may never be used for other purposes during סוכות.

phrases.english: Abaye and Rava, who both say:
It is where he says: I am not separating myself from them
during the entire twilight period,
so that holiness does not take effect on them.
But the wood of the sukkah,
on which holiness does take effect
is set aside for seven days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 15 and supports רב מנשיא's position from Step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing cases: decorations versus the סוכה's wood, and preventing holiness versus removing it
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A תנאי works on a סוכה של מצוה, as the decorations show.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תנאי on decorations works only by preventing holiness from starting at בין השמשות. The wood becomes holy no matter what and stays מוקצה for all seven days.

steps.title: Why is the סוכה different from seven אתרוגים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא compares the סוכה to someone who set aside seven אתרוגים, one for each day. There the holiness of each אתרוג lasts only one day, so why does the סוכה stay holy for all seven days?
steps.simpleTranslation: And how is this different from what was taught: if someone set aside seven אתרוגים, one for each of the seven days, רב said he fulfills the מצוה with each one and may eat it right away. רב אסי said he fulfills the מצוה with each one and may eat it the next day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea from Step 16 that the סוכה's wood is holy for all seven days. It points to a case where something set aside for the חג is holy only one day at a time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב and רב אסי argue about when you may eat each day's אתרוג: right after using it, or only the next day. But both agree that its holiness does not carry over into the whole חג. So why should the סוכה's holiness stretch across all seven days instead of renewing day by day?

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference? (a formula that asks why two similar cases are treated differently)
He set aside (designated something for a purpose)
Citrons used for the מצוה of the four species on סוכות

steps.confusionAlert: רב and רב אסי really do argue, but their argument is not the point here. The גמרא uses the part they agree on: an אתרוג's holiness is limited to its own day, not the whole חג.

phrases.english: And what is different from that which was stated:
phrases.notes: Introduces a comparison case to challenge the previous ruling.

phrases.english: If one set aside seven etrogim
for the seven days,
phrases.notes: One אתרוג for each day of the festival.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב: כׇּל אַחַת וְאַחַת יוֹצֵא בָּהּ
phrases.english: Rav said: with each and every one he fulfills his obligation
and he may eat it immediately.
phrases.notes: Once that day's מצוה is done, the אתרוג is no longer set aside.

phrases.english: And Rav Asi said:
with each one he fulfills his obligation
and he may eat it the next day!
phrases.notes: It stays set aside for its whole day, but not beyond. The exclamation marks this as a challenge.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling from Step 16 that the סוכה's wood is מוקצה for all seven days.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the holiness of the סוכה's wood lasts through all seven days of the חג.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: With seven אתרוגים set aside for the חג, each one's holiness covers only its own day. The סוכה should work the same way, with holiness that covers one day at a time and does not lock in for all seven days.

steps.title: Nights break up the אתרוג's days but not the סוכה's
steps.stepSummary: The מצוה of אתרוג is only by day, so each day is its own separate מצוה. The מצוה of סוכה applies at night too, so all seven days are like one long day.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, by אתרוג, the nights break up the days, so each day is a separate מצוה. Here, by סוכה, the nights do not break up the days, so all the days are like one long day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by showing that the two מצוות work differently. The אתרוג's מצוה stops every night, but the סוכה's מצוה never stops.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no אתרוג מצוה at night, so every day starts a brand-new מצוה, and each אתרוג is holy only for its own day. Living in the סוכה is a מצוה day and night, with no break in the middle. So the holiness never gets a chance to leave the wood until the whole חג ends.

keyTerms.meaning: Nights from days (the nights come between the days)
One long day: several days treated as one single unit

steps.whatToRemember: A מצוה that stops at night (אתרוג) is a new מצוה each day. A מצוה that goes on day and night (סוכה) makes all seven days into one long day. That is why the סוכה's wood stays holy and מוקצה until the end of the חג.
steps.whyThisMatters: The idea of יוֹמָא אֲרִיכְתָּא, one long day, is a useful tool. It shows that whether a מצוה is one continuous unit or a chain of separate daily מצוות can change the halacha.

phrases.english: There, where the nights interrupt between the days —
phrases.notes: "There" means the אתרוג, whose מצוה is only by day.

phrases.english: each and every day
is a מצוה on its own.
Here, where the nights do not interrupt between the days —
phrases.notes: "Here" means the סוכה, whose מצוה applies at night too.

phrases.english: all the days
are considered like one long day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from Step 17 by showing how אתרוג and סוכה are different.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (חילוק): the two מצוות have a different structure in time.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might have thought that the סוכה, like the אתרוגים, is holy only one day at a time.
steps.terutzMaskana: The סוכה's מצוה goes on without a break through the nights, so all seven days form one long day, and the wood stays holy until the חג ends.
